AP-01.finds: Vatican Necropolis Scavi (1939–49): 2nd-c. trophy monument under the high altar; contested bones in a niche. Constantinian memoria above earlier cemetery.
AP-01.authors: 1 Clement 5 (Peter & Paul suffered at Rome); Gaius via Eusebius HE 2.25 (Vatican tropaion); Tertullian Scorpiace 15; non-Christian Tacitus Annals 15.44 describes Nero’s Christian persecution after the fire (does not name Peter). || NON-CANONICAL / interpreter notes (not Holy Scripture): Thomas Horn; Cris Putnam:
AP-01.present: Present St Peter’s is Renaissance/Baroque over medieval/Constantinian footprint. Circus of Nero tradition for martyrdom nearby; necropolis preserved under basilica.

AP-03.finds: Cathedral crypt reliquary; archaeologists report early Christian cemetery under/near cathedral — not proven to be James son of Zebedee.
AP-03.authors: Acts 12 (death in Jerusalem). Compostela legend appears in medieval sources (e.g. rediscovery under Alfonso II tradition); not in Josephus/Tacitus. || NON-CANONICAL / interpreter notes (not Holy Scripture): Gabriele Boccaccini (Enoch Seminar circle):  | James C. VanderKam:
AP-03.present: Romanesque core with later Gothic/Baroque façades; major pilgrimage terminus (Camino).

AP-04.finds: Justinianic cross-in-square basilica ruins; traditional tomb chamber found empty in modern excavation.
AP-04.authors: Irenaeus (John lived into Trajan’s reign); Eusebius; Polycrates. Roman pagan authors do not narrate John’s burial. || NON-CANONICAL / interpreter notes (not Holy Scripture): L.A. Marzulli:  | Ken Johnson:
AP-04.present: Ruins on Ayasuluk Hill, Selçuk; fortress and İsa Bey Mosque nearby. Basilica ruined after medieval conquests.

AP-05.finds: Octagonal martyrium; nearby early church; 2011 D’Andria announcement of a tomb complex associated with Philip cult (identification debated).
AP-05.authors: Polycrates of Ephesus via Eusebius HE 3.31 (Philip at Hierapolis). Foxe’s ‘Heliopolis in Phrygia’ tracks this region.
AP-05.present: Ruins inside Hierapolis-Pamukkale UNESCO archaeological park; pilgrimage path to martyrium hill.

AP-13.finds: Marble sarcophagus under papal altar; slab tradition PAULO APOSTOLO MART; Constantinian then Theodosian basilica; 2006 window opening to tomb.
AP-13.authors: 1 Clement 5; Dionysius of Corinth via Eusebius; Tertullian (beheading analogy with John the Baptist); Acts ends with Paul under house arrest (no death scene).
AP-13.present: 19th-c. reconstruction after 1823 fire; tomb area conserved under altar. Tre Fontane abbey marks traditional beheading site separately.

AP-14.finds: Living Armenian patriarchal cathedral; traditional memorial of James — not a modern forensic excavation of 1st-c. bones.
AP-14.authors: Josephus Antiquities 20.9.1 (non-Christian): Ananus has James brother of Jesus stoned. Hegesippus via Eusebius adds fuller-club narrative. || NON-CANONICAL / interpreter notes (not Holy Scripture): Gabriele Boccaccini (Enoch Seminar circle):  | James C. VanderKam:
AP-14.present: Armenian Quarter cathedral complex; continuous liturgical use.
